symptom: The research-only two-socket fixture received an SCM_RIGHTS descriptor, then asserted payload and object admission before returning the FD. On a mismatched expected frame the assertion could raise while the received FD remained open, bypassing caller-side finally cleanup. An isolated Linux reproduction observed fstat succeeding on the received FD after the rejection. The patched receive-local finally closes it and a new live-process regression checks EBADF before exit. No production leak or attack is claimed.
lesson: SCM_RIGHTS descriptors are already installed in the receiver when recvmsg returns. If a helper checks flags, payload or identity and raises before returning the descriptor, cleanup in the caller after receive() is never reached. Process teardown masks this live-process descriptor leak. A receive-local ownership scope must close all parsed FDs on every failed admission before ownership is transferred.
guardrail: Wrap ancillary parsing and every pre-return admission check in exception-safe receive-local FD ownership; close all received descriptors on denial, and transfer ownership only after validation. Test an intentionally mismatched frame with fstat -> EBADF while the process remains alive. Reuse the existing SCM_RIGHTS close-on-reject, fd-lifetime and embedded-Python String.raw guardrails. Research-only; never connect production, Current BUY, LINE, public publishing, automated betting, Owner Dashboard, protected N2 or private raw evidence.
